Meta da aula. Ao final das quatro sessõe: Lesson goal. By the end of the four sessions, you put two objects in the right order (Ich gebe es ihm), put time, manner and place in order (Ich fahre morgen mit dem Zug nach Berlin), place nicht correctly, and know where the verb goes in every kind of sentence.
Os amigos se reúnem no aniversário de Ca: The friends get together for Camila's birthday.
— Feliz aniversário, Camila! Estou te da: — Happy birthday, Camila! I'm giving you this book.
— Que gentileza! Você mesmo escolheu?: — How kind! Did you pick it out yourself?
— Yes, I bought it last week in Berlin. My sister recommended it to me.
— E eu te dou amanhã o meu presente. Ain: — And I'll give you my present tomorrow. I haven't wrapped it yet.
— Vocês são muito queridos. Hoje à noite: — You're so sweet. Tonight I'll show it to my mom on a video call.
PASSO 1: o alemão pede a ordem dos prono: STEP 1: German has fixed orders for pronouns and nouns, and an order for time, manner and place — and that order is often the OPPOSITE of English. STEP 2: English says "I'm going to Berlin by train tomorrow" (place – manner – time). German says «Ich fahre morgen mit dem Zug nach Berlin» (time – manner – place: the "TeKaMoLo" rule: temporal, kausal, modal, lokal). STEP 3: with two pronouns, German matches English: "I gave it to him" = «Ich habe es ihm gegeben» (accusative first).
I gave it to the child.
I'm going to Berlin by train tomorrow.
I've lived in Berlin for two years.

Qual frase segue a ordem neutra usual, c: Which sentence follows the usual neutral order, with both objects as nouns: dative before accusative?
Quando os dois objetos são substantivos,: When both objects are nouns, dative before accusative is the usual neutral order in this example: dem Kind das Buch. «Das Buch dem Kind» can also be grammatical with a different focus; it isn't an absolute ban.
Qual frase segue a ordem neutra, com o p: Which sentence follows the neutral order, with the personal pronoun before the noun object?
Na ordem neutra, o pronome pessoal es pr: In neutral order, the personal pronoun «es» comes before the noun object «dem Kind»: Ich gebe es dem Kind.
Qual frase segue a ordem usual dos dois: Which sentence follows the usual order of two unstressed personal pronouns: accusative before dative?
Com dois pronomes pessoais átonos, a seq: With two unstressed personal pronouns, the usual order is accusative before dative: es ihm — just like English "it to him". So: Ich gebe es ihm.
Qual frase segue a sequência neutra temp: Which sentence follows the neutral order time → means of transport → destination?
A primeira frase segue a sequência neutr: The first sentence follows the neutral order taught here: morgen, time; mit dem Zug, means of transport; nach Berlin, destination. The order of these elements can vary with focus, and it isn't an absolute rule for every sentence — but it's the reverse of the usual English order.
Na negação da ação nesta frase com Perfe: To negate the action in this Perfekt sentence, «nicht» goes before the final participle: Ich habe das Buch nicht gelesen.
Para negar o predicativo müde, coloca-se: To negate the adjective «müde», put «nicht» before it: Er ist nicht müde (he isn't tired).
Ich habe keine Zeit, ___ komme ich nicht: Ich habe keine Zeit, ___ komme ich nicht.
Deshalb expressa consequência e ocupa a: «Deshalb» (that's why, so) expresses a consequence and takes first position in the second clause; the verb «komme» comes right after it. With «weil», the clause would have a different order: weil ich nicht komme.

Complete com deshalb, trotzdem ou außerd: Complete with deshalb, trotzdem or außerdem to express a concession ("anyway"): Es regnet, ___ gehen wir spazieren.
Trotzdem significa mesmo assim e marca a: «Trotzdem» means "anyway, nevertheless" and marks the concession: it's raining, and we're going for a walk anyway. The verb «gehen» comes right after «trotzdem».
Complete com deshalb, trotzdem ou außerd: Complete with deshalb, trotzdem or außerdem to express a consequence ("that's why"): Ich bin müde, ___ gehe ich nach Hause.
Deshalb significa por isso e apresenta a: «Deshalb» means "that's why, so" and introduces the consequence: I'm tired, so I'm going home. The verb «gehe» comes after «deshalb».
